duplicate_rows.rule: identical (ts, content_sha256, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens) within one file; first occurrence kept
duplicate_rows.rule_applicability: decidable only on the 9 rows files carrying content_sha256 and a millisecond ts; the 5 legacy-schema files have no content_sha256 and a second-resolution ts_utc, where the literal tuple over-merges demonstrably distinct requests (different rep, different latency_s)
cannot_distinguish: a genuine double-send with identical prompt and completion (improbable: two calls cannot share a client-measured ttft_s/latency_s and the same millisecond ts)
a retried or resumed request (it would carry a new ts, so the rule does not catch it by design)
near-duplicates with a different content_sha256 (none found)

assumptions.what: all 8 gradings use fixture LR-01.v5.json (3 checkpoints)
assumptions.why: it is the fixture the one pre-existing grade_v5 output used, so all 23 pairs share one declared space; LR-01.v6.json carries 12 checkpoints and would change the declared space mid-metric. Recorded as a coverage gap, not patched.

assumptions.what: grade files named cell-<gridtag>-<stamp>.grade-v5.json instead of cell-<arm>-<stamp>
assumptions.why: grade_v5 emits one file per rows file covering all arms; a single-arm name would be false for the 7 multi-arm grids, and tokens_to_verified.py maps these files by rows_file so nothing depends on the name.

assumptions.what: duplicate rule counted as decided only on files carrying content_sha256 and millisecond ts
assumptions.why: on the 5 legacy-schema files the literal tuple over-merges rows that differ in rep and latency_s; reporting 54 excess without that boundary would publish 24 fabricated duplicates.

assumptions.what: no ledger or latency report edited; corrected figures published in DUPLICATE-ROWS.md
assumptions.why: card forbids editing REQUEST-LEDGER.json / LATENCY-REPORT.json; the marker-name reconciliation is a publish decision, not arithmetic.
